title: derive manufactures FormalProof without checking entailment
evidence: Lines 223-240 check modality and premise verification only; lines 248-253 clone any goal and format premise text as a proof term. FormalProof is accepted for reproducibility/confidence at 179-195 without interpreting that term.
trigger: Call derive with a verified epistemic premise A and an unrelated epistemic goal B with Provenance, Reproducibility, Confidence and Completeness obligations.
impact: Returns a FormalProof that verify accepts for B although A does not entail B. This is an unsound proof API, not evidence of a protected runtime effect bypass.

title: Deduplicate statements by modality as well as content
evidence: seen_content stores only js.statement.content although Modality is a semantic field (45-49) and derive requires a Deontic premise (223-230).
trigger: Optimize two individually verified statements sharing content, first Epistemic then Deontic.
impact: Drops the Deontic premise; a subsequent Deontic derivation that previously passed fails HumeViolation, violating stated conservativity at 262/267.

title: Freshness obligation never checks observation age
evidence: has_freshness returns true for every non-Conjecture justification, including Observation timestamp 0. orchestrator.rs:67-88 accepts caller timestamps, calls verify and persists the observation. bindings.rs:179-182 constructs timestamp 0 and invokes verify.
trigger: Verify or inject an arbitrarily old Observation carrying Obligation::Freshness.
impact: The freshness guard passes stale observations and persists them as verified knowledge; no age policy or current-time comparison is performed.

title: Attestation generator signs hard-coded successful test results
evidence: test_results_data embeds SUPPORTED_WITHIN_DOMAIN, zero violations and suite pass counts (73-170); 174-180 serialize/hash them without invoking or loading test results.
trigger: Run the generator on an untested or failing checkout.
impact: It emits a cryptographically signed bundle presenting invented current test evidence and silicon certification.

title: Artifact verification compares two stored hashes without reading the artifact
evidence: Generated verifier sets artifact_hash_ok from artifact.sha256 == manifest artifact_hash; no artifact bytes or source tree are read (320-322).
trigger: Modify the released source/binary while preserving an existing bundle.
impact: Verifier still reports ARTIFACT HASH VERIFIED and can exit successfully; it cannot establish that the supplied implementation matches the attested artifact.

title: Environment provenance is hard-coded for every host
evidence: Only arch/os/release are observed; chip, filesystem, runtime, compiler, entropy and LOCAL_EMPIRICALLY_VERIFIED_SILICON are literals (188-194).
trigger: Run generator on another host or toolchain.
impact: Signed environment evidence misidentifies hardware/compiler/provenance, invalidating reproducibility claims.

title: In-process sandbox has no allocation or output bound
evidence: Whitelisted Mult/list/constant nodes permit x = [0] * 10**10; execution uses host-process exec and StringIO capture at 392–408 with no memory or output limit.
trigger: Execute a small AST allocating a huge list/string or producing large captured output.
impact: Untrusted generated code can exhaust host memory; an alarm does not bound allocation size or isolate process failure.

title: Ordinary generated-code errors escape ExecResult handling
evidence: The exception handler catches only ValueError, TypeError, OSError and KeyError; permitted expressions include division and unresolved Name nodes.
trigger: safe_exec receives 1 / 0 or an undefined identifier.
impact: ZeroDivisionError/NameError propagate to the caller instead of the documented failed ExecResult.

title: Verifier exits successfully after failed hash or signature checks
evidence: Lines 34 and 37-51 calculate failure flags; lines 66-73 only print them; main returns normally at line 76. Only missing files call sys.exit(1).
trigger: Run verifier on a complete bundle with mismatched binary.sha3 or invalid signature.
impact: Shell/CI consumers checking the exit status accept a failed verification as success.

title: Signed causal hash does not authenticate bundle metadata or artifact
evidence: Hash chain compares two copied strings; signature covers causal_hash_str only (48). ARTIFACT is VERIFIED whenever manifest is nonempty (66). commit.txt, claims.snapshot, timestamp and binary bytes are not hashed or bound to the signed value.
trigger: Modify claims.snapshot, environment.json, test-results.json or commit.txt in an otherwise valid signed bundle.
impact: The verifier can retain VERIFIED hash/signature/artifact rows while reporting attacker-modified provenance or claim counts; it does not verify the advertised bundle integrity.

title: Selector engine labels heuristics as measured optimality
evidence: evaluate_selector_fitness declares ÓPTIMO solely when active tier/effort equals infer_optimal_tier (427–438); generate_signature enables audit_selector by default (521,535–546).
trigger: Generate a signature with known model/mode whose tier matches the keyword classification.
impact: Output asserts optimality without comparative cost/time/error evidence, contrary to .babylon60rules model-and-presentation requirement. No selector mutation or execution bypass is alleged.

title: Missing effort metadata is replaced by a fabricated mode
evidence: parse_selector_string maps model-name words to Fast/High and otherwise returns Standard (108–114); detect_active_model_and_mode calls it even when effort variable is absent (151–163).
trigger: Provide OPENAI_MODEL but omit OPENAI_REASONING_EFFORT, or supply a hook model with no effort.
impact: Signatures present an inferred effort as sourced environment/hook metadata instead of preserving No expuesto, undermining model/effort provenance.

title: Return a lexical error for out-of-range integer literals
evidence: Lexer::next_token collects arbitrary-length decimal text and invokes num.parse().expect("BFT Fallback") rather than returning a recoverable error. Lexer and tokenize are public.
trigger: Pass an integer token larger than i64::MAX through Lexer::tokenize.
impact: Malformed source panics during lexing rather than producing a parser diagnostic; any caller without panic isolation loses its compilation request/process. No running service exposure established.

title: Stress harness reports success even when health transitions fail
evidence: saw_degraded, saw_dead and recovered are printed but never asserted; final line unconditionally prints empirical success.
trigger: The engine regresses to never enter Degraded/Dead or reset fails to restore Healthy while hash checks still pass.
impact: The harness exits successfully and announces passed falsification despite the very health transitions it promises to verify failing.

title: Effective resistance silently treats disconnected graphs as finite
evidence: The function accepts arbitrary nx.Graph, checks only node count, and always returns N*trace(pinv(L)). For two isolated vertices L and pinv(L) are zero, so the returned total resistance is zero although no intervertex conduction path exists.
trigger: Call compute_effective_resistance, or get_structural_debt_triple, on a disconnected graph with at least two vertices.
impact: Disconnected structure is assigned a finite, potentially zero total resistance and misleading structural-debt output. Scope is the exported analytical function; no control-policy consumer is asserted.

title: Returned SQLite cursor is attached to an already closed connection
evidence: execute_with_backoff returns cursor inside with self._connection(); the context manager finally closes conn at line 55. The batch method repeats this at lines 98 and 108.
trigger: A caller uses the advertised sqlite3.Cursor return value to fetch results from a SELECT or reuse the cursor.
impact: The returned cursor cannot fetch/re-execute after the context closes its connection. Existing located callers only write, so no current caller failure is asserted.

title: Unsigned short vector lengths underflow the SIMD loop bound
evidence: size_t len is used in j <= len - 16; AVX512 repeats j <= len - 64 at line 63. No preceding lower-bound guard. Caller traced: 01_KISH_ENGINE/babylon60/transducers/void_vec.py:77-90 passes len(query) directly with no minimum or batch element length checks; pack_void_bit at 94-116 permits arbitrary dimensions padded only to 8 bits.
trigger: Call exported NEON function with count > 0 and len < 16, or AVX512 function with len < 64.
impact: With an accelerator shared library present, public Python void_batch_hamming_dist/void_hamming_dist accepts short packed vectors and reaches the underflowing C loop, causing out-of-bounds reads and potential process crash. No caller minimum-length constraint was found.

title: Architecture manifest points its formal foundation to a missing proof path
evidence: The foundation and section 2 link docs/proof/lean/BabylonTrace.lean; a targeted read reports No such file or directory. The whitepaper instead links proof/lean/BabylonTrace.lean.
trigger: Follow the formal-foundation or bisimulation link from this manifest.
impact: Readers cannot inspect the cited proof through the documented reference.

title: Manuscript presents scripted simulation as empirical LLM comparison
evidence: Lines 115-132 describe independent LLM configurations, observed budget acknowledgements and proof of semantic failure. benchmarks/run_ablation_matrix.py:29-32 returns a fixed 1000 tokens; 67-70 explicitly programs the soft overshoot; 52 and 113 assign violation counts by formula/constant. The gate used there is Python (src/spinal_gate.py:82-98), whereas manuscript:106 claims native code.
trigger: Use the paper table and analysis as evidence for LLM budget compliance or native runtime confinement.
impact: Readers receive empirical and native-enforcement claims that this cited deterministic harness cannot establish; label results as simulation and remove unmeasured behavioral claims.

title: Disconnected Markov output is not strict JSON
evidence: Fallback returns surprisal_bits=float("inf"); CLI json.dumps uses default allow_nan and emits Infinity (lines1920 onward).
trigger: --json requested for disconnected origin/target.
impact: Output advertised as structured JSON cannot be parsed by strict JSON consumers.

title: Python-only counter loop is described as Rust FFI and SPMC validation
evidence: Header claims lock-free Python/Rust coupling; FFIWriter constructs a local ctypes structure (42), never loads a Rust library or starts a reader; run_stress_test only publishes sequentially and asserts counter parity (76-97). _pack_=1 is also not a cache-line alignment guarantee.
trigger: Use this demo success as evidence for the declared cross-language seqlock/SPMC property.
impact: The example cannot establish ABI coupling, concurrent reader coherence or lock-free ordering. No production caller was located by targeted search; finding is confined to example/evidence claims.

title: Push proceeds when neither biometric gate implementation is available
evidence: The command lookup / Swift-file conditional ends at line 193 without an else rejection; line 197 directly runs git push origin main. This is a direct effect consumer, not merely proposal admission.
trigger: A checkout has local commits ahead of origin/main and neither c5_biometric_gate on PATH nor the Swift source file is available.
impact: The script publishes commits without obtaining the hardware attestation it explicitly requires. The Swift file currently exists, so this is a missing-gate failure-mode defect, not a claim that the current checkout bypassed authentication.

title: Auditor follows file symlinks when rewriting targets
evidence: collect_targets accepts item.is_file() at line 60; audit_file uses stat/read_text/write_text at lines 75,83,101 without rejecting symlinks or checking target containment. run_swarm forwards collected paths with dry_run false by default.
trigger: A matching-extension symlink inside the audited tree points to a writable outside file containing a case variant of one replacement term, and the CLI runs without --dry-run.
impact: The advertised workspace audit can modify a file outside the selected root through the symlink.

title: Swarm release audit reports hard-coded successful checks
evidence: Z3 25/25, quality gate 103/103 and zero CVEs are printed unconditionally; ok4=True with no checks. The final ALL 4 FRONTS OPERATIONAL is printed even if earlier fronts failed, and __main__ ignores the returned boolean.
trigger: Run runner when checks fail or have not run.
impact: Automation receives exit status 0 and a success verdict without corresponding evidence.

title: Label generated swarm findings and metrics as synthetic in exported evidence
evidence: execute_agent selects a constant corpus item (line 92), adds sine/cosine perturbations to fixed scores (95-99), sleeps (102), and exports these as findings with exergy_score, kolmogorov_ratio and shannon_entropy (111-114,157-167). The JSON contains no synthetic/simulation qualifier; console calls them 100 concurrent agents.
trigger: Run the script and consume legion_100_results.json as the audit evidence suggested by its audit docstring.
impact: The output presents predetermined judgments and manufactured metric variations as agent audit results, with no source retrieval or measurement. It should explicitly mark simulation and avoid presenting fixed metrics as measured quantities. No downstream consumer or real agent execution is established.

title: Durability regression inspects a fresh SQLite connection
evidence: Test opens sqlite3.connect(sync_db) then reads PRAGMA synchronous; repeats with a fresh connection for actor_db at lines 57-62.
trigger: Remove or weaken the writer connection synchronous setting while SQLite fresh connections retain default FULL.
impact: The test still passes because synchronous is connection-local and it checks the reader default rather than either writer.

title: Queue HTTP examples acknowledge failed HTTP responses
evidence: Buffering API Calls awaits fetch then batch.ackAll without response.ok; Durable Objects example similarly ack() after stub.fetch without checking status.
trigger: Upstream responds 429 or 500 with a fulfilled fetch response.
impact: Consumer acknowledges unprocessed work and prevents queue retry.

title: Remove credential scavenging and autonomous secret injection directive
evidence: Exhaustión Autónoma de Credenciales instructs scanning 20_VAULT and neighboring repositories and autonomously injecting any discovered credential, before asking the user.
trigger: An agent applies this module while configuring an API and follows the credential search directive without authorization for neighboring repositories or use of discovered secrets.
impact: The document instructs access and secret use beyond task authorization; this conflicts with the canonical rule that retrieved instructions do not expand permissions. This report identifies an unsafe instruction, not an observed runtime bypass.

title: Backward conditioning uses the initial prior at the wrong timestep
evidence: For target_t < min(window), joint = pi0 * T_steps[:, observed] uses pi0 directly; it does not propagate pi0 to target_t.
trigger: pi0 describes timestep zero, target_t is positive, and the earliest observation is later than target_t in a nonstationary Markov chain.
impact: Posterior probabilities, hallucination rates and surprisal can be incorrect. The prior must first be advanced to the target timestep or its time origin made explicit.
